# 2 Chronicles Chapter 11 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** When Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he assembled 180,000 fighting men from Judah and Benjamin to wage war against Israel and win back the kingdom.

**2** But the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God:

**3** "Tell Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and all the Israelites in Judah and Benjamin:

**4** 'This is what the LORD says: Do not march out to fight your brothers. Every man go home, because this is My doing.'" They obeyed the LORD's word and turned back from attacking Jeroboam.

**5** Rehoboam stayed in Jerusalem and fortified cities throughout Judah for defense.

**6** He built up Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa,

**7** Beth-zur, Soco, Adullam,

**8** Gath, Mareshah, Ziph,

**9** Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah,

**10** Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron — all fortified cities in Judah and Benjamin.

**11** He reinforced the fortifications and stationed commanders in them, with supplies of food, olive oil, and wine.

**12** He placed shields and spears in every city and made them very strong. So Judah and Benjamin remained his.

**13** The priests and Levites from all over Israel sided with him.

**14** The Levites abandoned their pasturelands and property and moved to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons had rejected them as priests of the LORD.

**15** Jeroboam had appointed his own priests for the high places, for the goat-demon idols, and for the calf idols he had made.

**16** People from every tribe of Israel who were determined to seek the LORD, the God of Israel, followed the Levites to Jerusalem to offer sacrifices to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.

**17** They strengthened the kingdom of Judah and supported Rehoboam son of Solomon for three years, walking in the ways of David and Solomon during that time.

**18** Rehoboam married Mahalath, the daughter of David's son Jerimoth and of Abihail, the daughter of Jesse's son Eliab.

**19** She bore him sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.

**20** After her, he married Maacah daughter of Absalom, who bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.

**21** Rehoboam loved Maacah daughter of Absalom more than any of his other wives and concubines. In all, he had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and he fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.

**22** Rehoboam designated Abijah son of Maacah as crown prince among his brothers, intending to make him the next king.

**23** He acted wisely, dispersing his sons throughout Judah and Benjamin — stationing them in all the fortified cities. He provided them generously and obtained many wives for them.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **11:4**: "This is My doing" — God takes ownership of what looks like political disaster. The Chronicler insists that even the breakup of the kingdom is under God's control.

- **11:14-16**: The Chronicler describes a kind of reverse exodus: faithful Levites and Israelites leave the north and migrate south. True Israel isn't about geography — it's about allegiance to YHWH.

- **11:23**: Rehoboam shows genuine political savvy here — dispersing his sons to prevent a succession crisis, keeping them well-provided and occupied. He's a better administrator than he is a theologian.


— PNEUMA
